title: Case Study: LLM Copilot with Tools + RAG
interviewAnswer: Keep numerical/business logic deterministic in tools, use the LLM for orchestration and explanation, use RAG only for unstructured knowledge, and evaluate tool correctness separately from language quality.
why: This case shows modern LLM engineering without using the model for tasks that deterministic tools can perform more reliably.
intuition: Let the LLM orchestrate and explain; let trusted tools calculate. Use RAG for unstructured knowledge and tool calls for structured business logic.
deepDive: The agent interprets intent, calls deterministic forecasting/inventory functions, optionally retrieves policy/meeting-note context from a vector store, and synthesizes the response. Keep tool schemas explicit, separate retrieval quality from generation quality, log traces, and evaluate both factual/tool correctness and usefulness. MCP can expose the same capabilities to multiple compatible clients.
workedExample: Question requiring a deterministic calculation → agent calls a trusted domain tool → structured result returned → LLM explains assumptions. Question about policy or documentation → retrieve relevant chunks → answer with grounded context and citations.
commonMistakes: Letting the LLM invent numerical forecasts that a deterministic model should compute.
Calling every document query “RAG” without retrieval evaluation.
Assuming an agent should autonomously act without permission boundaries.
followUps: Why tool calling instead of pure prompting?
production: Add authentication, tool permissions, structured outputs, tracing, retries/timeouts, prompt/model versioning, retrieval evaluation, cost/latency budgets and a safe fallback when the LLM or external provider fails.
